subject: Acme Pharm — follow-up: data handling & PII for prompt outputs
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 15:02:00 +0000
Subject: Acme Pharm — follow-up: data handling & PII for prompt outputs

Hi Priya — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on what we discussed related to prompt/output data: 

- Scope: your prototype will send product descriptions + customer-provided notes to Redwood for generation and post-processing (no direct PHI expected in the POC, but you may surface limited PII fields in prompts/outputs).
- What we store: by default Redwood does not store prompt text or generated outputs for customer-owned private deployments. For Hosted (Redwood API) we provided options — telemetry (for infra and billing) vs. optional retention for quality/monitoring. You indicated you need a clear guarantee on what is persisted.
- Residency: you want US-only physical residency for any persisted artifacts.
- Retention: Acme's security team asked about 30/90/365 day retention options for any retained logs or outputs and an export mechanism.
- Audit: you required audit logs showing who accessed logs and model runs.

Attached: a concise dataflow diagram and a SOC2 summary to help legal/security triage.

Next steps (proposed):
1) I will confirm exact retention options and defaults for Hosted vs. Private by EOD tomorrow (18 Apr).
2) Marissa will prepare a preliminary commercial note on Dedicated vs Hosted cost delta if you decide to avoid retention on Hosted.
3) If you agree, we can schedule a 30-min follow-up with your security and legal on Tue (20 Apr) to sign off on residency + retention constraints.

Can you confirm that covers the open items and whether Tue morning works for you?

Thanks — Alex

--

Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 09:18:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Acme Pharm — follow-up: data handling & PII for prompt outputs

Thanks Alex — that summary is helpful. A couple quick clarifications from security/legal before we lock the follow-up: 

1) For Hosted API: when you say "optional retention for quality/monitoring", can you confirm what fields are retained (prompt text, model output, metadata such as IP, user id, timestamps)? Are prompts/outputs ever used for model improvement/replication?

2) Retention policy granularity: can we set retention separately for prompts vs outputs vs debug logs? Our default preference is: do not retain prompts or outputs beyond 7 days unless explicitly opted-in, but retain infra/debug logs for 90 days for troubleshooting.

3) Residency: we need an explicit guarantee that any retained artifacts for Acme (if we opt in) will be stored only in the US and will not be replicated outside the US for backup without notice. Is that achievable on Hosted, or would we need Dedicated/Private?

4) Audit and export: we need an automated export (S3-compatible) of retained items and audit records, and a retention-deletion confirmation event for compliance reporting.

If you can respond to these specific bullets, I can loop in Sam (legal) to attend the Tue call.

Best,
Priya
Director of Product Security — Acme Pharmaceutics
priya.shah@acmepharm.com

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acmepharm.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 13:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Acme Pharm — follow-up: data handling & PII for prompt outputs

Priya — great questions. Answers below, plus concrete ops items and timing. Quoting your bullets for clarity:

> 1) For Hosted API: when you say "optional retention for quality/monitoring", can you confirm what fields are retained (prompt text, model output, metadata such as IP, user id, timestamps)? Are prompts/outputs ever used for model improvement/replication?

- Hosted default (no retention): we persist only billing and infra telemetry (request timestamp, model id, token counts, latency metrics). This telemetry is aggregated and not customer-identifying.
- Hosted with retention opt-in: we can persist prompt text, model output, and request metadata (timestamp, customer API key id, region) for troubleshooting and quality monitoring. We do NOT use any customer prompts or outputs to train or improve our public models unless a customer explicitly opts into a separate "training consent" agreement. That is a contractual opt-in and requires legal approval.

> 2) Retention policy granularity: can we set retention separately for prompts vs outputs vs debug logs? Our default preference is: do not retain prompts or outputs beyond 7 days unless explicitly opted-in, but retain infra/debug logs for 90 days for troubleshooting.

- Yes, retention is configurable per artifact type. We support retention windows at the artifact level (prompts, outputs, kv/debug logs, audit trails). Typical options: 7d / 30d / 90d / 365d / indefinite. For Hosted opt-in customers we can apply a 7d prompt/output retention and 90d infra/debug retention as you described.

> 3) Residency: we need an explicit guarantee that any retained artifacts for Acme (if we opt in) will be stored only in the US and will not be replicated outside the US for backup without notice. Is that achievable on Hosted, or would we need Dedicated/Private?

- Hosted: we can pin the storage region to US-only for retained artifacts and backups — we will provide contractual language specifying that persisted artifacts are stored in US region(s) only and not replicated outside the US without prior written consent. Note: certain platform control-plane metadata (non-content telemetry) may be routed for operational purposes to our global control plane; we will list those fields separately in the contract appendix.
- Dedicated/Private: if you require stricter physical control and an isolated control plane (no Redwood-managed control-plane routing), Dedicated or Private is available and is the recommended route for strict regulatory needs. We'll detail tradeoffs (cost, SLA) in the follow-up.

> 4) Audit and export: we need an automated export (S3-compatible) of retained items and audit records, and a retention-deletion confirmation event for compliance reporting.

- Export: supported. We can configure scheduled exports to your S3 bucket (or a tokenized presigned URL pattern) for retained prompts/outputs and audit logs.
- Deletion confirmation: we provide deletion events and a retention lifecycle report (signed) on request; for Hosted customers this is a standard add-on in our compliance package.

Operational items and timing:
- Today EOD (19 Apr): I attached the dataflow and SOC2 summary you already have.
- Tue 20 Apr 10:00–10:30 PT: proposed security & legal call to confirm contractual language and residency wording. Does that work for you and Sam?
- Wed 21 Apr: Marissa will prepare a cost delta memo for Hosted-with-opt-in (7d prompts/90d infra) vs Dedicated with no retention.

Let me know if you want any of the retention windows customized further — we can include that in the exhibit.

Thanks — Alex

--
Alex Martinez

- For the export: confirm the export format schema (field names and encryption at rest in S3). Ideally we get an S3 manifest + gzipped ndjson for contents and a separate armored audit log with access events.
- For retention/deletion confirmations: can Redwood provide a signed timestamped attestation after deletion events? If that requires an add-on fee, let us know.

If you can drop links to sample clause language and an export schema prior to 10:00 PT, that will make the call most productive.
